Test Steps: 1. Open the ledger with a wide date range. 2. Export CSV. 3. Compare totals and dates against the screen.
Expected Result: Every transaction in range is exported, and amounts and dates match the on-screen ledger exactly.

Test Steps: 1. Create an order whose customer name holds a comma and a double quote. 2. Export CSV. 3. Open the file in Google Sheets.
Expected Result: The row parses into the correct columns with the punctuation intact. No field bleeds into the next column.

Element / Feature: Assign a pickup to an agent
Test Steps: 1. Open an unassigned pickup. 2. Pick an active agent. 3. Assign. 4. Check the agent's own job list.
Test Data: Any unassigned pickup; an active agent
Expected Result: The order advances automatically, shows the agent's name badge, and appears under that agent's jobs.

Test Steps: 1. Open the agent picker. 2. Look for an inactive agent. 3. Try to assign one via the API.
Test Data: One active agent, one inactive agent
Expected Result: Inactive agents do not appear in the picker, and assigning one through the API is refused with a clear message.

Test Steps: 1. Open the same order as two admins. 2. Assign different agents at the same instant.
Test Data: One order id; admin A picks agent 1, admin B picks agent 2
Expected Result: One assignment wins under the shared guard. The other admin is told the order already moved, and the order carries exactly one agent.

Test Steps: 1. Open an order in a late status. 2. Check every section and the timestamps.
Test Data: An order in status weighed or settled
Expected Result: Customer, sender, receiver, parcel, payment, agent, status history and documents all render, with every date in IST.

Test Steps: 1. Open the verifications view. 2. Open one account's documents. 3. Check the access log.
Test Data: An account with documents pending review
Expected Result: Pending accounts are listed, documents open for review, and each open is recorded in the access log.

Test Steps: 1. Open /ops/users. 2. Read the roles. 3. Change a role if the control is offered.
Expected Result: Staff users and their roles render correctly, and any offered role change takes effect.

Test Steps: 1. Approve one pending request. 2. Reject another. 3. Check both orders and the customer's view.
Expected Result: The approved order becomes cancelled, the rejected one keeps its status, and the customer sees each outcome.

Test Steps: 1. As a customer navigate to /ops/dashboard. 2. Call GET /api/ops/orders directly.
Expected Result: The navigation is bounced by SurfaceGuard and the API call is refused by requireRole on the server.

Test Steps: 1. Note a date and amount on a card. 2. Compare it in the table, on the detail page and in the CSV.
Test Data: One order carrying a known timestamp and amount
Expected Result: All four render the same IST date and the same INR-formatted amount. No UTC drift and no raw number formatting.

Element / Feature: Today filter uses the IST day
Test Steps: 1. Set the clock to 00:30 IST. 2. Filter booking date by today. 3. Check an order booked at 23:30 IST yesterday and one at 00:10 IST today.
Test Data: Clock 00:30 IST; one order at 23:30 yesterday, one at 00:10 today
Expected Result: Only the 00:10 order is included. The boundary is 00:00 IST, not 00:00 UTC.

Test Steps: 1. Toggle the sort. 2. Check the first and last rows. 3. Export and check the file order.
Expected Result: The order reverses correctly on screen and the CSV export follows the same order.

Test Steps: 1. Trigger events on an order. 2. Open /notifications. 3. Read one. 4. Check the badge.
Test Data: An order moving through two or three statuses
Expected Result: Notifications list newest first and the unread count drops by one when a notification is read.

Test Steps: 1. Set WA_DRY_RUN=1. 2. Trigger a notifying order event. 3. Read the log and the table. 4. Check the recipient's phone.
Expected Result: The message is rendered and logged and a whatsapp_messages row is written, but nothing is delivered to the phone.

Test Steps: 1. Unset TATA_WA_TOKEN. 2. Trigger a notification. 3. Request a login OTP. 4. Check /notifications.
Expected Result: Sends are skipped and logged, in-app notifications still work, and the login OTP falls back to the server console.

Test Steps: 1. POST each receipt type. 2. POST a STOP message from a number. 3. Trigger a send to that number.
Test Data: Receipts: sent, delivered, read, failed. Then body STOP
Expected Result: Each receipt updates the message row, and after STOP that number receives no further sends.

Test Steps: 1. POST to the path with a wrong final segment. 2. POST to the correct one.
Expected Result: The wrong secret is refused. The path segment is the entire authentication on this endpoint.

Element / Feature: SMS fallback for the login OTP
Test Steps: 1. Force a WhatsApp OTP delivery failure. 2. Request a login code. 3. Read the log.
Expected Result: The SMS fallback is attempted and the gap is logged loudly. NOTE: no SMS vendor is wired yet, so expect the logged failure, not a delivered SMS.

Test Steps: 1. Call each ops endpoint signed out. 2. Repeat as a customer. 3. Repeat as an agent. 4. Repeat as an admin.
Test Data: orders, orders/export, payments, payments/export, cancellations, orders/:id, orders/:id/assign, verifications, users
Expected Result: The first three are refused on every endpoint. Only admin and super_admin succeed.

Test Steps: 1. Call the agent endpoints as a customer. 2. Repeat as an agent.
Expected Result: The customer is refused on all three. The agent succeeds.

Test Steps: 1. Sign in. 2. Edit the session cookie value in devtools. 3. Reload.
Test Data: SESSION_SECRET set to a real random value; cookie edited by one character
Expected Result: The tampered session is rejected and the browser is signed out rather than acting as another user.

Test Steps: 1. As an agent open /ops and /home. 2. As an admin open /agent. 3. As a customer open /ops and /agent.
Test Data: One agent, one admin and one customer session
Expected Result: Each is bounced to their own surface. Confirm the matching server APIs also refuse - the guard is cosmetic on its own.

Test Steps: 1. Complete a signup with documents. 2. Query the three tables directly. 3. Read document_no and file_data.
Test Data: Direct psql or Supabase SQL access
Expected Result: document_no and file_data are ciphertext. No readable Aadhaar or PAN number appears in any column.

Test Steps: 1. Open a document as ops. 2. Open it again as the owner. 3. Read the access log table.
Expected Result: Both accesses are recorded with who viewed it and when.

Test Steps: 1. Change the account phone to a new number and verify it. 2. Try to sign in with the old number. 3. Unlink the phone.
Expected Result: The new number requires its own OTP and works. The old number no longer signs in to that account.

Test Steps: 1. Deploy integration/testing to Vercel. 2. Load the app. 3. Exercise one API call. 4. Read the function logs.
Test Data: Vercel project with the full env set
Expected Result: The app serves as a serverless function with no module-resolution error - relative imports carry the extension Node needs.

Test Steps: 1. Deploy without REDIS_URL. 2. Sign in. 3. Navigate across several pages over a few minutes.
Expected Result: The session persists via the Postgres store or signed cookies. The user is never signed out at random between invocations.

Test Steps: 1. List the environment variables on the customer-facing deployment. 2. Check each of the four flags.
Expected Result: All four are unset. Each is honoured in production builds, so any one left set is a live security hole.

Test Steps: 1. Open the support FAB. 2. Ask a question. 3. Ask a follow-up. 4. Press New session.
Test Data: OPENAI_API_KEY set; question: How do I track my shipment?
Expected Result: A reply is returned, the follow-up keeps the earlier context, and New session clears the history.

Test Steps: 1. Send messages as fast as possible. 2. Watch for the limiter.
Expected Result: The limiter engages with a clear message rather than failing silently or hanging.
